subject: Private upgrade: compact maintenance window & escape-hatch readiness
body:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acmeretail.com, devops@cloudvendor.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private upgrade: compact maintenance window & escape-hatch readiness

Hi team,

Per our call last week, we are preparing a short, low-risk maintenance window to apply the 2026.Q3 security and runtime patches to Acme Retail's private VPC deployment. Goal is a compact, scripted change that completes within a 90-minute window (target 02:00-03:30 UTC) to minimize retail hours impact.

Attached: acme_maintenance_constraints.pdf with customer constraints and compact-window-ops-checklist.xlsx with the initial ops checklist. Also attaching escape-hatch-scripts.tar.gz draft for pre-approved rollback helpers.

Key asks:
- Acme: confirm blackout windows and any additional network ACLs that must remain static during the patch (ops@acmeretail.com).
- CloudVendor: confirm that the host-level maintenance (hypervisor livepatch) is available during our window and whether any networking flips are expected (devops@cloudvendor.com).
- Redwood infra: Karthik, Monica, can you validate the proposed KV-cache pinning strategy and that model-serving agents will accept the staged version flag without requiring a full image re-pull?

Draft timeline (UTC):
1) 01:30 - preflight checks, snapshot + artifact push
2) 02:00 - begin node-level patching (rolling, cordon)
3) 02:40 - service health validation, smoke tests
4) 03:00 - quick load validation, uncordon any healthy nodes
5) 03:20 - final telemetry check and sign-off

Fallback/escape-hatch: If any critical latency or error spike >5% P99 token latency within smoke, we will trigger immediate automated rollback using the attached scripts. We will also unpin any in-flight sessions using the model-version-circuit breaker.

Avery
Avery Johnson
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

--

From: ops@acmeretail.com <ops@acmeretail.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: devops@cloudvendor.com
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 02:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private upgrade: compact maintenance window & escape-hatch readiness

Avery,

Thanks — confirmed on our side that the 02:00-03:30 UTC window is acceptable for regional stores (low traffic). A couple of constraints we captured in the attached PDF:
- No ACL changes allowed during 01:50-03:40 UTC; transit routes must remain stable.
- Any planned restart of host agents must be announced 30 minutes prior to avoid scheduler collisions with nightly batch jobs.

We also cannot tolerate more than 2% store-failure rate during the window; if we see more than 2% errors in checkout services we'll need to halt.

Ops (Acme)

--

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, ops@acmeretail.com, devops@cloudvendor.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 07:06:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private upgrade: compact maintenance window & escape-hatch readiness

Thanks for the constraints — noted. A few technical clarifications on our side so we can finalize the runbook: 

1) Version pinning approach: we'll implement a short-lived pin at the route-level (service config override) that forces traffic to model-variant v1.9.2 while we patch nodes. This avoids forcing a container image re-pull for each model container and keeps KV caches warm for pinned sessions. Pin will expire automatically after 4 hours unless extended.

2) Rolling strategy: we will cordon 1 node at a time per AZ, drain L7 traffic with our native drain hooks, run the OS/runtime patch, and run a container fast-health restart. Expected per-node window: 8-12 minutes.

3) Telemetry thresholds: our smoke tests will check 3 things — startup errors, P50/P95 token latency, and end-to-end request success %. If any metric deviates beyond the configured gates (startup errors >0; P95 increase >25% baseline; success rate <98%), an automated abort flag will be set.

4) Escape hatch details: the escape-hatch-scripts.tar.gz contains (a) automated rollback that re-applies previous service config and model pins, (b) KV cache warmers to pre-populate hot prefixes, and (c) a tracer restart to clear corrupted RPC channels. We recommend we stage these scripts on s3://acme-maint/staging prior to window.

I'll update the runbook and push a versioned checklist. Monica — can you confirm the playbook will update the model-serving agent with the pin without needing a full redeploy?

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

--

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, ops@acmeretail.com, devops@cloudvendor.com
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private upgrade: compact maintenance window & escape-hatch readiness

Confirmed — pin will be a lightweight service-config flag; agent will accept the override and maintain existing container images. Implementation notes: 
- We will atomically write the pin to the control plane config store, and each agent will reconcile on the next sync (sub-30s).
- Rollback uses the same mechanism in reverse; the scripts also include a forced cache-warm path that issues benign prefix calls to rebuild KV entries.

Added a small checklist item: snapshot the on-disk model shard index prior to node drain. That helps in case we need to do an emergency state restore. I attached compact-window-ops-checklist.xlsx with an updated snapshot step.

Also, one operational ask for CloudVendor: please confirm whether live-migration is enabled on these hosts; if so we need to prefer cordon+drain versus forcing crash-restart to avoid hidden IOPS spikes.

Monica
Monica Patel
SRE Manager | Redwood Inference

--

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, ops@acmeretail.com
Cc: devops@cloudvendor.com
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private upgrade: compact maintenance window & escape-hatch readiness

Runbook link and preflight checklist updated: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDefG-maintenance-plan (please do not share externally).

I've versioned the runbook as v20260904-compact and included the following additions:
- Exact CLI sequence for pinning/unpinning (command snippets)
- Health-check endpoints and example curl/assert commands
- A small python-based smoke harness that hits a representative set of prefixes and validates success rate.

I also added JIRA ticket JIRA-OPS-1248 for post-mortem and rollback audit. Please review and ACK by EOD PST so we can finalize the change window.

Neha Kapoor
Engineering Reliability | Redwood Inference

--

From: ops@acmeretail.com <ops@acmeretail.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: devops@cloudvendor.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 04 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private upgrade: compact maintenance window & escape-hatch readiness

Thanks all — ACK from Acme. We reviewed the runbook and constraints; we will stage the s3 artifacts and confirm live-migration status with CloudVendor tomorrow morning. If everything looks clean we'll send a final maintenance advisory to store ops by EOD.

Regards,
Sam Rodgers
Head of Ops | Acme Retail
